items.title: William Russell Interview, 1976-02-16
items.q: I talked to both of them once

ctx.x: this aspect of the origins of jazz is completely a non-reading that call response pattern is completely outside the reading tradition and that plays a big part in it of course.

I think it was Bud Scott too told me in California, that was 1940 when I talked to him in 39, maybe 1940 that winter I was there. Bolden used to take these twin sisters Nora and Dora Bass to a church, it was a Baptist church supposedly, which doesn't always have the best music, usually some of the, well as you'd call them, sanctified churches or things like Church of God and Christ that have more dancing and instrumental music in them than the Baptists usually. But, anyway, speaking of the Bass sisters, I talked…
Most musicians at that time too were now doing the music full-time, were they?

items.title: Betty Lee Hanson, Joe James, George Lewis, Joe Lewis, Joe Butler, Kid Thomas Valentine, Bill Russell, Allan…
items.q: He used to take his girlfriend whom he later married with, either Nora or Dora Bass. There were two twins.

ctx.x: Well, how important was the religious feeling in influencing all of this? Well, I think that's difficult to say, too.

Of course, for people like me that came down here years after it started, I would never know. But other people like, say, Kid Ori, for instance, and some of the first people I met in California, like Bud Scott, one of the old-timers, quite a few of those said that a lot of the music came right out of the churches of the jazz bands as if... I know it was either Ori or Bud Scott. I don't remember which one. It could have been Mutt Carey. I'm talking about Buddy Bolden. They said, well, he got all of his music right…
What about the street marches, the funeral marches? Are they all the same thing?
